tagline: Delivering reliable energy, natural gas and water infrastructure to support sustainable growth in the Northeast
hero_kpi_rationale: CAPEX is the primary driver of regulated growth for Eversource, with $26.51 billion projected from 2026 to 2030, concentrated on electric networks, gas infrastructure and resilience, positioning the company as a key player in critical infrastructure across New England.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Amount invested each year in infrastructure such as electric and gas networks.
kpis.description: Capital investments in 2025 totaled $4.16 billion, down from $4.48 billion in 2024. A plan of $26.51 billion is projected from 2026 to 2030.
kpis.signal: CAPEX declining in 2025 but planned at $26.51 billion over 2026-2030, demonstrating strong commitment to regulated infrastructure.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from the company's operating activities.
kpis.description: Operating cash flows reached $4.11 billion in 2025, compared to $2.16 billion in 2024.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in operating cash flows from 2024 to 2025, reflecting better operational performance.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share (non-GAAP)
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to shareholders divided by the average number of diluted shares outstanding, excluding exceptional charges.
kpis.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $4.76 in 2025, compared to $4.57 in 2024. Long-term EPS growth is projected between 5% and 7% from 2025 to 2030.
kpis.signal: Non-GAAP EPS growing, reflecting improved operational performance after excluding charges related to offshore wind and Aquarion sale.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Total amount of dividends distributed per ordinary share.
kpis.description: Dividends paid in 2025 were $3.01 per share, compared to $2.86 per share in 2024. The approved quarterly dividend for 2026 is $0.7875 per share.
kpis.signal: Dividend increasing, reflecting management confidence in stable cash flows and growth prospects.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenues and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin is not explicitly mentioned in the provided 10-K excerpts. Regulated utilities operate under a regulated rate-setting model without a traditional gross margin concept.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenues.
kpis.description: Operating margin is not directly provided in the excerpts. Regulated utilities operate under a regulated rate structure rather than business margins.

kpis.name: R&D Investments
kpis.description: No data on R&D spending found in the documents. Regulated utilities allocate innovation spending through regulated CAPEX.
kpis.signal: Not available: regulated utilities invest minimally in traditional R&D.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Employee count is not mentioned in the provided MD&A and Financial Statements sections of the 10-K.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends for the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.788 last year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow for the last 4 fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $1.101 billion last year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated for the last 3 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 65.0% last year.

kpis.name: Regulated Revenue Base
kpis.explanation: Growth in revenues from regulated segments (electricity, natural gas, water).
kpis.description: Eversource benefits from favorable regulatory decisions in 2025 (PSNH +$100.7 million, Yankee Gas +$95.7 million, NSTAR Gas rate reset), supporting regulated revenue growth.
kpis.signal: Growth driven by favorable regulatory decisions and capital investments.

kpis.name: Infrastructure Investment Plan
kpis.explanation: Planned investment in critical infrastructure and network modernization.
kpis.description: Eversource projects a massive investment plan including $1.23 billion for information technology and facilities improvements and enhancements, positioning the company in infrastructure digitalization and resilience.
kpis.signal: Ambitious investment plan of $26.51 billion from 2026 to 2030, including $11.24 billion in electric distribution, $6.80 billion in natural gas and $7.24 billion in electric transmission.

kpis.name: Dividend Growth
kpis.explanation: Progressive increase in dividends paid to shareholders.
kpis.description: The quarterly dividend increased from $0.715 in 2024 to $0.7525 in 2025, and is approved at $0.7875 for 2026, reflecting steady growth aligned with EPS growth prospects.
kpis.signal: Quarterly dividend increase to $0.7875 for 2026, reflecting confidence in cash generation and earnings sustainability.

kpis.name: Favorable Regulatory Framework
kpis.explanation: Positive impact of regulatory decisions on revenues and profitability.
kpis.description: State regulators (NHPUC, PURA, DPU) approved rate increases and alternative regulatory frameworks, notably the annual alternative regulatory framework for PSNH and continuation of the PBR program for NSTAR Gas through 2030.
kpis.signal: Multiple favorable regulatory decisions in 2025 and 2026 support growth and improve visibility.

risks.title: AI-Assisted Cyberattacks
risks.score_rationale: The company is vulnerable to sophisticated cyberattacks including AI, which could compromise critical electric transmission and distribution, gas and water systems. Potential impact on operations and reputation is significant.

risks.title: Regulation and Authorized Rates
risks.score_rationale: Regulatory decisions directly impact revenues and profitability. Regulators may deny rate increases or impose stricter standards, affecting economic viability.

risks.title: Energy Supplier Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on third-party suppliers for natural gas and energy supply. Factors such as inflation, supply tariffs and geopolitical conflicts can affect costs.

risks.title: Operational Reliability and Performance
risks.score_rationale: Service reliability is essential. System failures, outages or service interruptions can damage reputation and result in regulatory penalties.

risks.title: Environmental Compliance and Energy Transition
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to increasingly strict environmental regulations regarding greenhouse gas emissions and water quality. Compliance and energy transition costs can be significant.

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Critical Infrastructure Security
risks.score_rationale: Geopolitical conflicts increase risks of cyberattacks against critical infrastructure and can affect supply costs through trade sanctions and supply chain disruptions.

risks.title: Aquarion Sale and Regulatory Uncertainty
risks.score_rationale: PURA initially rejected the Aquarion sale in November 2025. A court appeal was approved in January 2026, with a decision expected in March 2026. This uncertainty affects strategy and cash flows.

ai_positioning.summary: Eversource mentions AI-assisted cyberattacks as a growing risk in its 10-K report, but does not yet have major public initiatives for AI deployment in operations. The company acknowledges that cyberthreats are increasing in sophistication including AI, and plans to invest in information technology in its 2026-2030 investment plan.
evidence: Cyberattacks that seek to exploit potential vulnerabilities in the utility industry are increasing in sophistication including artificial intelligence
Plan to invest $1.23 billion in information technology and facilities upgrades and enhancements from 2026-2030
